note: Recorded once, from the frozen, already-verified content of cde/lib/metrics.js and cde/analysis/lib/*.js — the same files cde/phase5/preflight.js's no_phase4_or_5_redefinition_of_locked_metrics check exists to protect. That check normally answers 'has any Phase 4/5 commit touched these files?' via `git log -- <path>`, which needs real commit history. On a shallow clone (git fetch --depth=1, Render confirmed) that query is structurally unable to see history and always reports the latest fetched commit as touching every path, regardless of content — a hosting artifact, not a tamper signal. demo/server/integrity.js falls back to this content hash only when that happens, answering the same underlying question ('do these files match the frozen, tested record?') in a way that does not depend on clone depth. Regenerate only if these files are genuinely, disclosedly changed again — never to make a check pass.
